title: Guidelines for representing your business on Google
measures: Eligibility and naming rules for Business Profiles, including chains and brands (consistent names and categories), one profile per location, individual practitioners (dentists named as an example), phone numbers that connect to the individual location and websites that represent it.
limitations: Policy page; Google may change it without notice. Undated on the page.

title: Verify Business Profiles in bulk
measures: Bulk verification eligibility: 10 or more profiles of the same business (duplicate, suspended or disabled profiles do not count), not a service-area business, spreadsheet must include all managed profiles; agencies with more than one business in one account cannot bulk verify; Google may de-verify accounts that do not actively manage profiles.
limitations: Help article; requirements and the Business Profile Manager interface change over time. Undated on the page.

title: Create & manage business groups
measures: What business groups are, when to use them instead of shared logins, transferring profiles into groups, and the tradeoff between one group and several groups (access scope versus separate spreadsheets and dashboards).
limitations: Help article; interface steps may change. Undated on the page.

title: Manage business group owners & managers
measures: Business group roles: multiple owners but one primary owner; only owners manage users, delete or transfer the group; managers can add, edit and delete all profiles in the group but cannot manage users; Google Groups cannot be owners or managers.
limitations: Help article; role names and capabilities may change. Undated on the page.

title: Manage your Business Profile owners & managers
measures: Individual profile roles: owners have full control and one primary owner; managers have mostly the same access but cannot add or remove users or remove the profile.
limitations: Help article. Undated on the page.

title: Add & manage Business Profile store codes for bulk uploads
measures: Each location needs a unique, stable store code before a spreadsheet import; adding or changing a store code for an existing location via spreadsheet creates a duplicate location.
limitations: Help article. Undated on the page.

title: Tips to improve your local ranking on Google
measures: Google's description of local results as based mainly on relevance, distance and prominence (also described on the page as popularity).
limitations: High-level description; Google does not publish weights. Undated on the page.

title: Site moves with URL changes
measures: Google's site-move process: URL mapping, server-side permanent redirects (301/308), avoiding redirect chains, Search Console verification of old and new sites, Change of Address tool, expecting temporary ranking fluctuation, a few weeks or more for medium-sized sites, keeping redirects generally at least one year.
limitations: Page last updated 2026-08-20 per the page footer; Google may revise it.

title: Web Vitals
measures: Core Web Vitals thresholds: LCP within 2.5 seconds, INP of 200 milliseconds or less, CLS of 0.1 or less, assessed at the 75th percentile of page loads segmented by mobile and desktop; INP replaced FID as a stable Core Web Vital in 2024; lab tools cannot measure INP.
limitations: Last updated 2024-10-31 per the page; metric set can change.

title: Understanding Core Web Vitals and Google search results
measures: Google recommends achieving good Core Web Vitals; they align with what core ranking systems seek to reward alongside other page experience aspects.
limitations: Last updated 2025-12-10 per the page footer. Does not quantify ranking effect.

title: Understanding page experience in Google Search results
measures: Core ranking systems look to reward good page experience across many aspects; Google seeks to show the most relevant content even if page experience is sub-par.
limitations: Last updated 2026-09-22 per the page footer. Qualitative guidance only.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
measures: The WCAG 2.2 Recommendation (12 December 2024 version), including criteria new in 2.2 such as 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum, AA), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA), 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, AA: at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels with exceptions), 3.2.6 Consistent Help (A), 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A) and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum, AA); W3C advises using WCAG 2.2.
limitations: A technical standard, not a law. Conformance claims require evaluation of full pages and processes.

title: Guidance on Web Accessibility and the ADA
publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division (ADA.gov)
measures: DOJ's position that Title III covers businesses open to the public, listing medical offices among examples; that DOJ has no regulation setting detailed web standards for businesses; that businesses have flexibility in how they comply but must make online goods and services accessible; WCAG and Section 508 cited as helpful technical standards.
limitations: Informal, non-binding guidance dated 18 March 2022; the page states it may be rescinded or modified and does not reflect the separate April 2024 Title II rule for state and local governments. Not legal advice.

title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
measures: Google's self-assessment questions for people-first content, the warning signs of search engine-first content, E-E-A-T and extra weight on YMYL topics such as health, and the Who, How and Why framing including bylines, avoiding fabricated author profiles, and disclosure of automation where readers would expect it.
limitations: Last updated 2026-10-05 per the page footer. E-E-A-T is described as not itself a specific ranking factor.

title: Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content
measures: Google rewards quality however content is produced; using automation including AI primarily to manipulate rankings violates spam policies; appropriate use of AI is not against guidelines; on health topics systems place even greater emphasis on reliability signals.
limitations: Blog post from February 2023; later documentation (generative AI guidance, spam policies) should be read alongside it.

title: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website
measures: Generative AI can help research and structure original content; generating many pages without adding value may violate the scaled content abuse policy; focus on accuracy, quality and relevance and fact-check and review AI-generated content before publishing.
limitations: Last updated 2026-10-01 per the page footer.

title: Spam policies for Google web search
measures: Definition of scaled content abuse: many pages generated primarily to manipulate rankings and not help users, no matter how created, including using generative AI to generate many pages without adding value.
limitations: Last updated 2026-08-28 per the page footer; policies change.
